body.prompt:
Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L04_A, a medium-wide exterior view from the waiting lane facing the Old Blue Gate, showing the small service doorway open for a handover. Later views of the bench (L04_B) reuse this plate.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved Old Blue Gate master, exterior waiting lane at night. Use it for: the exact gate architecture and orientation: two monumental indigo timber leaves with brass celestial ornament and a central sun disc, pale carved-stone piers, the two carved stone figures on the pier tops, layered blue-and-gold arches, burgundy drapery, blue star banners, warm hanging lanterns, the round full-moon ornament on top, the small left equipment exit gate, the planter with white flowers, the blue-and-brass bench, the hedges and the wet pale paving. Ignore and never reproduce: its painted title at the top-left and every white annotation label box, annotation word and arrow.
Camera and framing: the master's orientation, frontal from the waiting lane at standing eye height, medium-wide. The whole gate is centred. Screen-left edge: the separate small blue equipment exit gate, beyond the left stone pier. Then the planter in front of the left pier. Centre: the two main leaves. Screen-right: the right pier and the blue-and-brass bench. The lower third of the frame is open foreground paving.
Place and construction:
1. The small service door is cut into the LEFT main leaf, near the left pier, with the master's height, frame width and existing brass hinges.
2. The service door threshold is flush with the paving, no step.
3. The separate equipment exit is farther left, beyond the left stone pier, at the far-left edge of the frame.
4. The planter stays left, in front of the left pier. The bench stays right, beside the right pier.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Both main gate leaves: closed, their centre join tight and visible.
2. Service door in the left leaf: open inward on its hinges, revealing a narrow warmly lit interior threshold and inner floor behind it.
3. Equipment exit at far left: closed.
4. Bench seat: empty and clear.
5. Paving immediately outside the service door: clear handover space.
6. Beside that space, on the planter side and outside the swing of the service door: a clear empty trolley stopping bay of open paving.
7. Foreground lane: open and empty.
Physical inscriptions: none. No letters, numbers or words anywhere.
Keep clear and visible: the service door hinges and threshold, the lit inner floor behind the opening, the paving just outside it, the clear bay beside it, the main-door join, the equipment exit, both carved figures, the open foreground lane.
Light: all lanterns lit warm amber; warm light reaches the wet stone paving beneath cool blue night shadows; full moon ornament glowing as in the master.
Do not show: the service door in the right leaf; an open main gate; an open equipment exit; a trolley, cart or objects in the bays; any person, hand or animal; the master's title, label boxes, words or arrows.

Look and finish (same for every ChandRush location plate): premium semi-realistic painterly 2.5D graphic-novel illustration that matches the supplied ChandRush masters, a blend of illustration and reality. It is painterly in finish but crisp and precise in drawing. Materials and light have near-photographic conviction while forms stay clean, idealised and orderly, like a high-end storybook. ChandRush is an ancient travelling fair with grand, mystic, magical scale and real architectural detailing: dimensional deep-indigo and ultramarine painted timber with visible grain, joinery, rivets and edge banding; warm polished and cast brass with bright specular edges and a light patina; pale cream stone worktops and pale irregular stone paving with a light wet sheen and crisp reflections; layered fabric canopies; restrained circular celestial ornament (full-moon discs, rings, small eight-point stars) in gold and brass. Palette: ultramarine, cobalt, indigo and navy against amber, honey-gold and brass, with strong warm-cool contrast, saturated but natural, never neon. Light: fixed amber task lamps cast clean, well-defined warm pools, their glow held tight around the lamp glass with no spreading halo; cool full-moon light edges roofs, canopy gaps, stone and brass; deep, rich shadows that keep readable detail. Clarity: clear, dry night air with no haze, fog, mist, smoke or airborne dust. Crisp edges and high micro-contrast. Sharp, clean textures in wood grain, brass and stone, as in a high-resolution photograph. True deep darks and clean colours, never a milky, washed-out or glowing veil over the image, never soft focus. The background stays crisp and only slightly darker with distance. Ornament is dense above eye level and on frames; floors, worktops and mechanisms stay open, clean and readable.

Production rules (apply to every plate):
- Frame: one 4:3 landscape scenic image filling the whole canvas edge to edge. No border, title band, panel frame, vignette box or blank margin.
- Lettering: the only lettering allowed is the physical inscriptions listed above, rendered exactly as written, letter for letter, with each minus sign as a true minus sign. No other words, numbers or symbols anywhere. No title, caption, callout, label box, leader line, arrow, legend, watermark or signature: titles and callouts are added later by the production team.
- Reference images: their titles, annotation words, label boxes and arrows only identify places for you. Reproduce none of them.
- Empty location: no people, children, helpers, wooden figures, animals, hands, shadows of figures or silhouettes. The place waits, ready for characters to be added later.
- Counts and states are exact as stated. Add no extra copies of any counted object and no extra devices, cards, lamps or tiles.
- Unlit means unlit: clear or smoky glass with no flame, no inner glow and no bloom. Lit lamps glow only at their own glass.
- Avoid: haze, fog, mist, bloom halos, soft focus, a low-contrast or milky wash, modern signage, plastic, neon, sci-fi screens, crowds, text on fabric or banners, mirrored or garbled lettering, duplicated objects, warped or melted geometry, a second moon in the sky, a crescent moon.

Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L06_A, a directional view from just outside Food Street's Return Walk doorway, looking along the Covered Return Walk towards Entry Court, used as a delivery trolley route.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved Covered Return Walk master. Use it for: the viewing direction, passage width, the outer boundary wall with bracket lamps, planters and climbing plants on screen-right, the open fair-facing colonnade of blue timber posts on screen-left, post spacing, blue starred timber roof with hanging lanterns, the arched Entry Court approach at the far end under the full moon, and the wet pale paving. Ignore and never reproduce: every white annotation label box, annotation word and arrow.
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it for: the indigo timber, brass edging and jamb thickness of the Food Street side doorway, and the paving level. Ignore and never reproduce: its painted title, every white label box, annotation word and arrow, and all its counters, carts and objects.
Camera and framing: standing eye height, just outside Food Street's Return Walk doorway, looking straight along the covered passage towards Entry Court as in Image 1. The open Food Street doorway jamb (indigo timber with brass edging) stands in the near screen-left foreground, with a glimpse of the lit Food Street interior through the open side door. Several roof posts recede towards the Entry Court arch at the far centre. Outer boundary wall on screen-right, open colonnade on screen-left as in Image 1.
Place and construction:
1. The doorway threshold is level with the passage paving, no step.
2. The pale paved route runs clear along its full visible length.
3. The central path is wide enough for a delivery trolley, with a continuous walking strip alongside it on the outer-wall (screen-right) side.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Food Street side door: open.
2. Passage: completely empty, no trolley, crates or objects on the paving.
3. Entry Court arch visible at the far end.
Physical inscriptions: none. No letters, numbers or words anywhere.
Keep clear and visible: the level paving immediately outside the doorway, the clear centre of the passage, the walking strip along the right side.
Light: warm amber pools under the fixed bracket lamps and hanging lanterns; cool full-moon light through the open colonnade.
Do not show: a step at the threshold; objects in the passage; any person, hand or animal; titles, label boxes, words or arrows from the references.

Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L07_A, a wide view from the far Food Street threshold into the Parade Ground rehearsal yard. The elephant work area close-up (L07_B) reuses this plate.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved Parade Ground master. Use it for: the camera position and yard layout: the roped pedestrian lane with brass stanchions, blue rope and star banners on screen-left running towards the Moon Square counting arch at the far left-centre, the costume bench beside the left lane, the open central rehearsal loop, the blue elephant float with gold trappings on the right, the upper-right equipment gallery with railings, the near stair on the right, the rear walkway, lamps, bunting and the full moon. Ignore and never reproduce: every white annotation label box, annotation word and arrow.
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it for: the indigo shutter frame, brass edging and pale paving level of the threshold. Ignore and never reproduce: its painted title, every white label box, annotation word and arrow, and all its counters and objects.
Camera and framing: as Image 1, standing eye height at the far Food Street threshold looking straight into the yard. The raised shutter's indigo jambs with brass edging frame the left and right edges, and its raised shutter box frames the top. A strip of threshold paving fills the bottom of the frame. Left: visitor lane. Centre: rehearsal loop. Right: elephant work area, gallery and stair.
Place and construction:
1. The roped pedestrian lane runs along the left towards the Moon Square counting arch.
2. The costume bench stands beside the left lane, outside the loop.
3. The rehearsal loop is open paving in the centre.
4. The blue elephant float stands in the right work area at the master's position and scale.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Shutter: fully raised, only its bottom edge visible at the top.
2. Rehearsal loop and pedestrian lane: clear and empty.
3. Elephant float: stationary. Its wheels are visibly undersized, clearly too small for the big body. The master's temporary wooden supports stand under it. Every wheel and every support foot touches the paving, with grounded contact shadows.
4. A clear inspection patch of open paving lies beside the float, outside the supports, on the loop side.
Physical inscriptions: none. No letters, numbers or words anywhere.
Keep clear and visible: the paving just inside the shutter frame, the walkway inside the left rope, the clear patch beside the float, the rope boundary, the wheel and support contacts.
Light: warm amber work lamps illuminate the yard; cool full-moon edges on roof and gallery.
Do not show: large normal-size wheels; a float without supports; floating wheels or supports; objects in the loop; any person, hand or animal; titles, label boxes, words or arrows from the references.
